docs.title: Vellum
docs.text:
The Precision ODM for Asynchronous MongoDB & Pydantic.

Vellum is a type-safe, async Python ODM for MongoDB built on Pydantic v2 and Motor. It provides a clean repository pattern, fluent aggregation builder, lifecycle hooks, optimistic concurrency, soft deletes, and transactions — all with full type hints.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Description Type-safe queries Expression classes for all MongoDB operators (Eq, Gt, In, Regex, ElemMatch, Text Search, Geospatial, ...) Fluent field references Write Product.price < 10 or Product.fields.price < 10 Fluent aggregation AggregationPipeline with match, group, project, sort, unwind, lookup, add_fields, count Lifecycle hooks before_insert, after_insert, before_update, ... on your model Optimistic concurrency OptimisticConcurrencyMixin — automatic version-based conflict detection Soft delete SoftDeleteMixin — automatic filtering, soft_delete() / restore() Transactions async with repo.transaction() as session: FastAPI integration repository_factory for Depends injection Aggregation output models Validate aggregation results with Pydantic models Migrations MigrationRunner with up/down, status, rollback Caching CachedRepository with configurable TTL and invalidation Encryption EncryptedField / encrypted_field — Fernet-based field encryption Schema Doctor SchemaDoctor — check and repair schema conformance Seeding Seeder / Factory — generate test data Change streams ChangeStream — watch MongoDB change events Telemetry TracedRepository — wrap repository with tracing

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
import asyncio
from motor.motor_asyncio import AsyncIOMotorClient
from vellum import VellumBaseModel, VellumRepository

# 1. Define a model
class Product(VellumBaseModel):
    name: str
    price: float

    class Settings:
        collection_name = "products"

async def main():
    # 2. Connect
    client = AsyncIOMotorClient("mongodb://localhost:27017")
    db = client["myapp"]
    repo = VellumRepository(Product, db)

    # 3. Create
    product = Product(name="Widget", price=9.99)
    created = await repo.create(product)
    print(f"Created: {created.id}")

    # 4. Read
    fetched = await repo.get(created.id)
    print(f"Fetched: {fetched.name}")

    # 5. Update
    fetched.price = 24.99
    updated = await repo.update(fetched.id, fetched)

    # 6. Query with field references
    results = await repo.find(
        (Product.price >= 10.0).to_mongo_query()
    )

    # 7. Delete
    await repo.delete(created.id)

    client.close()

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Lifecycle Hooks
docs.text:
Override hook methods on your model to run logic automatically:

class AuditedItem(VellumBaseModel):
    name: str

    async def before_insert(self) -> None:
        print(f"About to insert {self.name}")

    async def after_insert(self) -> None:
        print(f"Inserted {self.name}")

    async def before_update(self) -> None:
        print(f"About to update {self.name}")

    async def after_update(self) -> None:
        print(f"Updated {self.name}")

    async def before_delete(self) -> None:
        print(f"About to delete {self.name}")

    async def after_delete(self) -> None:
        print(f"Deleted {self.name}")

Hooks are called automatically by repo.create(), repo.update(), repo.delete().

To cancel an operation, raise HookError in a before_* hook:

from vellum import HookError

async def before_insert(self) -> None:
    if not self.name:
        raise HookError("Name is required")

docs.title: Optimistic Concurrency
docs.text:
Prevent lost updates with version-based conflict detection:

from vellum import OptimisticConcurrencyMixin, OptimisticLockError

class Product(OptimisticConcurrencyMixin, VellumBaseModel):
    name: str
    stock: int

    class Settings:
        collection_name = "products"

p = Product(name="Widget", stock=100)
await repo.create(p)           # version = 1

p.stock = 90
await repo.update(p.id, p)     # version increments to 2

# If another update uses stale version → OptimisticLockError

docs.title: Soft Delete
docs.text:
Mark documents as deleted without removing them:

from vellum import SoftDeleteMixin

class Post(SoftDeleteMixin, VellumBaseModel):
    title: str

    class Settings:
        collection_name = "posts"

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
# Soft delete (sets deleted_at)
await repo.soft_delete(post.id)

# Find excludes soft-deleted by default
results = await repo.find()       # no deleted posts
post = await repo.get(post.id)    # raises DocumentNotFoundError

# Include deleted
results = await repo.find(include_deleted=True)

# Restore
await repo.restore(post.id)

docs.title: Count
docs.text: count = await repo.count()  # excludes soft-deleted

docs.title: Transactions
docs.text:
Requires a MongoDB replica set.

async with repo.transaction() as session:
    account_a.balance -= 100
    account_b.balance += 100
    await repo.update(account_a.id, account_a, session=session)
    await repo.update(account_b.id, account_b, session=session)
    # Auto-commits on success, rolls back on error

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text:
from vellum import MigrationRunner, SimpleMigration

async def add_field(db):
    await db.users.update_many({}, {"$set": {"role": "user"}})

async def remove_field(db):
    await db.users.update_many({}, {"$unset": {"role": ""}})

migration = SimpleMigration(1, "add role field", add_field, remove_field)

runner = MigrationRunner(db)
applied = await runner.run([migration])
rolled_back = await runner.rollback(1)
status = await runner.get_applied()

docs.title: Schema Doctor
docs.text:
Check and repair schema conformance:

from vellum import SchemaDoctor

doctor = SchemaDoctor[Product](Product, db)
report = await doctor.check()
print(report.issue_count)  # documents with issues

# Repair
await doctor.repair(dry_run=True)  # preview changes
await doctor.repair()              # apply fixes

docs.title: FastAPI Integration
docs.text:
from fastapi import FastAPI, Depends
from vellum import repository_factory, get_database

app = FastAPI()

@app.on_event("startup")
async def startup():
    app.state.db = await get_database("mongodb://localhost:27017/myapp")

@app.get("/products/{product_id}")
async def get_product(
    product_id: str,
    repo = Depends(repository_factory(Product)),
):
    return await repo.get(product_id)

docs.title: Seeding
docs.text:
Generate test data:

from vellum import Seeder, Factory

seeder = Seeder(db)

# With builder function
items = await seeder.seed(
    Product, count=5,
    builder=lambda i: {"name": f"Product {i}", "price": i * 10.0},
)

# With factory
factory = Factory(Product, lambda i: {"name": f"Prod {i}", "price": float(i)})
items = await seeder.seed(Product, count=3, factory=factory)

docs.title: Change Streams
docs.text:
Watch real-time changes:

from vellum import ChangeStream

stream = ChangeStream(repo.collection)

async for event in stream:
    print(f"Operation: {event.operation_type}")
    print(f"Document: {event.document}")

With wildcard handlers:

async def on_insert(event):
    print(f"Inserted: {event.document_key}")

stream = ChangeStream(repo.collection, handlers={"insert": on_insert})
await stream.watch()

docs.title: Telemetry
docs.text:
Wrap any repository for tracing:

from vellum import TracedRepository

traced = TracedRepository(repo)
# All operations are traced; use with OpenTelemetry or similar

docs.title: Aggregation Pipeline
docs.text: Build MongoDB aggregation pipelines with a fluent builder.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
from vellum import AggregationPipeline

pipeline = AggregationPipeline(repo.collection)

docs.title: $match
docs.text: results = await pipeline.match({"status": "active"}).execute()

docs.title: $group
docs.text:
results = await (
    pipeline
    .group("$category", total={"$sum": 1}, avg_price={"$avg": "$price"})
    .execute()
)

docs.title: $project
docs.text: results = await pipeline.project({"name": 1, "price": 1, "_id": 0}).execute()

docs.title: $sort
docs.text:
from vellum import FieldRef

quantity = FieldRef("quantity")
results = await pipeline.sort(quantity.desc()).execute()
# Or: pipeline.sort([("quantity", -1)])

docs.title: $limit / $skip
docs.text: results = await pipeline.sort(quantity.desc()).limit(5).skip(10).execute()

docs.title: $unwind
docs.text:
results = await pipeline.unwind("$items").execute()
# With options: pipeline.unwind({"path": "$items", "preserveNullAndEmptyArrays": True})

docs.title: $lookup (join)
docs.text:
results = await (
    pipeline
    .lookup(
        from_collection="orders",
        local_field="user_id",
        foreign_field="_id",
        as_field="orders",
    )
    .execute()
)

docs.title: $addFields
docs.text: results = await pipeline.add_fields({"total": {"$multiply": ["$price", "$quantity"]}}).execute()

docs.title: $count
docs.text:
results = await pipeline.count("total").execute()
# Returns [{"total": 42}]

docs.title: Output Models
docs.text:
Validate aggregation results with Pydantic models:

from pydantic import BaseModel

class RevenueByCategory(BaseModel):
    category: str
    total_revenue: float

results = await (
    pipeline
    .group("$category", total_revenue={"$sum": "$revenue"})
    .sort([("total_revenue", -1)])
    .execute(output_model=RevenueByCategory)
)
# results: list[RevenueByCategory]

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python >= 3.12
  • MongoDB >= 4.0 (transactions require a replica set)
  • motor, pymongo, pydantic (installed automatically)

docs.title: Install
docs.text: pip install vellum-odm

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
Vellum depends on:

Package Version Purpose pydantic >= 2.0 Data validation and settings motor >= 3.2, < 4.0 Async MongoDB driver pymongo >= 4.0, < 5.0 Sync MongoDB driver (used by Motor) cryptography >= 44.0 Fernet encryption for EncryptedField

cd Vellum
python -m venv .venv

pip install -e ".[dev]"

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
from vellum import VellumBaseModel
print(f"Vellum {VellumBaseModel.__module__}")

docs.title: Defining a Model
docs.text:
Models extend VellumBaseModel and use standard Pydantic v2 field declarations:

from vellum import VellumBaseModel

class Product(VellumBaseModel):
    name: str
    price: float
    tags: list[str] = []
    metadata: dict = {}

Every model automatically includes:

Field Type Description id UUID Auto-generated primary key (stored as _id in MongoDB) created_at datetime UTC timestamp set on creation updated_at datetime UTC timestamp updated on every change

docs.title: Collection Name
docs.text:
Set a custom collection name via the inner Settings class:

class Product(VellumBaseModel):
    name: str

    class Settings:
        collection_name = "products"

If collection_name is not set, it defaults to the lowercase class name (product).

docs.title: Serialization
docs.text:
# MongoDB-ready dict (id as string, by_alias)
doc = product.to_mongo()
# {"_id": "uuid-string", "name": "Widget", ...}

# Restore from MongoDB dict
restored = Product.from_mongo(doc)

docs.title: Optimistic Concurrency
docs.text:
from vellum import OptimisticConcurrencyMixin

class Product(OptimisticConcurrencyMixin, VellumBaseModel):
    name: str

Adds a version: int = 1 field. The repository auto-increments it on update and raises OptimisticLockError on stale writes.

docs.title: Soft Delete
docs.text:
from vellum import SoftDeleteMixin

class Post(SoftDeleteMixin, VellumBaseModel):
    title: str

Adds deleted_at: datetime | None. Soft-deleted documents are excluded from find() and get() by default. See Soft Delete for details.

docs.title: Both Together
docs.text:
class VersionedPost(OptimisticConcurrencyMixin, SoftDeleteMixin, VellumBaseModel):
    title: str

Order matters — OptimisticConcurrencyMixin first, then SoftDeleteMixin, then VellumBaseModel.

docs.title: Field References
docs.text:
Vellum provides two equivalent ways to reference model fields for queries and sorts:

# Direct syntax (Beanie-style)
Product.price > 10
Product.name == "Widget"

# Fields proxy syntax
Product.fields.price > 10
Product.fields.name == "Widget"

Both produce the same QueryExpression objects. See Queries for details.

docs.title: Indexes
docs.text:
Define indexes in Settings:

class Product(VellumBaseModel):
    name: str
    email: str

    class Settings:
        collection_name = "products"
        indexes = [
            {"key": [("name", 1)]},
            {"key": [("email", 1)], "unique": True},
        ]

Create them with:

await repo.ensure_indexes()

docs.title: Encryption
docs.text:
Encrypt individual fields transparently:

from vellum import encrypted_field

class User(VellumBaseModel):
    name: str
    ssn: encrypted_field("your-passphrase")  # auto encrypt/decrypt

Uses PBKDF2HMAC-SHA256 + Fernet symmetric encryption. Values are encrypted on serialization and decrypted on load.

docs.title: Queries
docs.text: Vellum supports MongoDB query operators through Python expressions. You can build queries using field references and compose them with &, |, and ~.

docs.title: Field References
docs.text:
Two equivalent syntaxes:

# Direct (Beanie-style) — requires Python 3.12+
Product.price > 10

# Fields proxy — always available
Product.fields.price > 10

Both return QueryExpression objects that compile to MongoDB query dicts via .to_mongo_query().

docs.title: Comparison Operators
docs.text:
Product.price == 10.0      # {"price": 10.0}
Product.price != 10.0      # {"price": {"$ne": 10.0}}
Product.price > 10.0       # {"price": {"$gt": 10.0}}
Product.price >= 10.0      # {"price": {"$gte": 10.0}}
Product.price < 20.0       # {"price": {"$lt": 20.0}}
Product.price <= 20.0      # {"price": {"$lte": 20.0}}

docs.title: Array & Set Operators
docs.text:
Product.name.in_(["A", "B"])         # {"name": {"$in": ["A", "B"]}}
Product.name.not_in(["A", "B"])      # {"name": {"$nin": ["A", "B"]}}
Product.tags.size(3)                 # {"tags": {"$size": 3}}
Product.tags.all_(["python", "mongo"])  # {"tags": {"$all": ["python", "mongo"]}}

docs.title: Element Operators
docs.text:
Product.email.exists()               # {"email": {"$exists": True}}
Product.email.exists(False)          # {"email": {"$exists": False}}

docs.title: String Operators
docs.text:
Product.name.regex("^Widget")              # {"name": {"$regex": "^Widget"}}
Product.name.regex("^widget", options="i") # {"name": {"$regex": "^widget", "$options": "i"}}

docs.title: Sub-document / Embedded Fields
docs.text:
Product.fields.address.city == "NYC"    # {"address.city": "NYC"}
Product.fields.address.state != "CA"    # {"address.state": {"$ne": "CA"}}

Direct syntax doesn't support chaining for nested fields — use FieldRef("address.city") or the fields proxy.

docs.title: ElemMatch
docs.text:
from vellum import Gt

inner = Gt("score", 90)
Product.grades.elem_match(inner)    # {"grades": {"$elemMatch": {"score": {"$gt": 90}}}}

docs.title: Geospatial Operators
docs.text:
# $near
Product.location.near((-73.97, 40.77), max_distance=1000)
Product.location.near((-73.97, 40.77), min_distance=100)

# $nearSphere
Product.location.near_sphere((-73.97, 40.77), max_distance=500)

# $geoWithin
polygon = {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[...]]}
Product.location.geo_within(polygon)

# $geoIntersects
Product.location.geo_intersects(polygon)

docs.title: Logical Composition
docs.text:
Combine expressions with & (AND), | (OR), and ~ (NOT):

# AND
(Product.price >= 10.0) & (Product.price <= 30.0)

# OR
(Product.name == "A") | (Product.name == "B")

# NOT (converted to $nor)
~(Product.name == "Widget")

# Mixed
((Product.price >= 10) & (Product.price <= 30)) | (Product.name == "Sale")

docs.title: Text Search
docs.text:
from vellum import TextSearch

TextSearch("hello").to_mongo_query()
TextSearch("hello", language="en", case_sensitive=True).to_mongo_query()

docs.title: Using Queries with Repository
docs.text:
Pass the compiled query dict to repository methods:

# As dict
results = await repo.find({"price": {"$gt": 10.0}})

# As expression
expr = (Product.price >= 10.0) & (Product.price <= 30.0)
results = await repo.find(expr.to_mongo_query())

docs.title: Sorting
docs.text:
# Ascending
+Product.price      # SortSpec("price", 1)
Product.price.asc()

# Descending
-Product.price      # SortSpec("price", -1)
Product.price.desc()

# With repository
results = await repo.find(
    sort=[Product.price.asc()]
)

docs.title: Free-function Equivalents
docs.text:
All operators also work as standalone functions:

from vellum import gt, eq, lt, in_, regex, near, exists

query = (gt("price", 10) & lt("price", 30)).to_mongo_query()

docs.title: Repository
docs.text: The repository pattern provides a clean abstraction over MongoDB collection operations.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
from motor.motor_asyncio import AsyncIOMotorClient
from vellum import VellumBaseModel, VellumRepository

class Product(VellumBaseModel):
    name: str
    price: float

    class Settings:
        collection_name = "products"

client = AsyncIOMotorClient("mongodb://localhost:27017")
db = client["myapp"]
repo = VellumRepository(Product, db)

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
product = Product(name="Widget", price=9.99)
created = await repo.create(product)

docs.title: Read
docs.text:
# By ID
fetched = await repo.get(product.id)

# Get raises DocumentNotFoundError if missing
from vellum import DocumentNotFoundError
try:
    await repo.get(uuid4())
except DocumentNotFoundError:
    pass

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
product.price = 24.99
updated = await repo.update(product.id, product)

docs.title: Delete
docs.text:
deleted = await repo.delete(product.id)  # returns True
# Raises DocumentNotFoundError if not found

docs.title: Find
docs.text:
# All documents
all_products = await repo.find()

# With filter dict
cheap = await repo.find({"price": {"$lt": 20.0}})

# With sort
results = await repo.find(sort=[+Product.price])

# With pagination
results = await repo.find(skip=10, limit=20)

docs.title: Find One
docs.text:
product = await repo.find_one({"name": "Widget"})
# Returns None if not found

docs.title: Find or Create
docs.text:
# Returns existing or creates new
product = await repo.find_or_create(
    {"name": "Widget"},
    defaults={"price": 9.99},
)

docs.title: Upsert
docs.text:
# Replaces document if exists, inserts if not
product = await repo.upsert(
    {"name": "Widget"},
    Product(name="Widget", price=19.99),
)

docs.title: Count
docs.text:
total = await repo.count()
filtered = await repo.count({"price": {"$gt": 10.0}})

docs.title: Bulk Operations
docs.text:
# Bulk create
products = [Product(name=f"Item {i}", price=i * 10) for i in range(5)]
await repo.bulk_create(products)

# Bulk update (matching filter)
await repo.bulk_update({"price": {"$lt": 20}}, {"$set": {"price": 20}})

# Bulk delete (matching filter)
await repo.bulk_delete({"price": 0})

docs.title: Indexes
docs.text:
# Create index
await repo.create_index([("email", 1)], unique=True)

# List indexes
indexes = await repo.list_indexes()

# Drop index
await repo.drop_index("email_1")

# Ensure indexes defined in Settings
await repo.ensure_indexes()

docs.title: Transactions
docs.text:
Requires a MongoDB replica set.

async with repo.transaction() as session:
    await repo.create(product, session=session)
    await repo.update(product.id, product, session=session)

docs.title: Cached Repository
docs.text:
Wraps any repository with an in-memory cache:

from vellum import CachedRepository

cached_repo = CachedRepository(repo, ttl=300)  # 5 minute TTL

# First call hits DB, second returns cached
await cached_repo.get(product.id)
await cached_repo.get(product.id)  # from cache

# Invalidate
cached_repo.invalidate(product.id)

docs.title: Traced Repository
docs.text:
Wraps any repository with telemetry spans:

from vellum import TracedRepository

traced_repo = TracedRepository(repo)

docs.title: Updates
docs.text: Use UpdateBuilder for fine-grained MongoDB update operations.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
from vellum import UpdateBuilder

builder = UpdateBuilder(repo.collection, doc_id)

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
# $set — set a field value
await (UpdateBuilder(repo.collection, doc_id)
    .set(Product.price, 29.99)
    .execute()
)

# $unset — remove a field
await (UpdateBuilder(repo.collection, doc_id)
    .unset(Product.tags)
    .execute()
)

# $inc — increment a numeric field
await (UpdateBuilder(repo.collection, doc_id)
    .inc(Product.quantity, 1)
    .execute()
)

# $push — add to an array field
await (UpdateBuilder(repo.collection, doc_id)
    .push(Product.tags, "new-tag")
    .execute()
)

# $pull — remove from an array field
await (UpdateBuilder(repo.collection, doc_id)
    .pull(Product.tags, "old-tag")
    .execute()
)

docs.title: Chaining
docs.text:
updated_doc = await (
    UpdateBuilder(repo.collection, doc_id)
    .set(Product.price, 29.99)
    .inc(Product.stock, -1)
    .push(Product.tags, "sold")
    .execute()
)

docs.title: Automatic Timestamps
docs.text: UpdateBuilder automatically adds updated_at to the $set operation, keeping the model's timestamp in sync.

docs.title: With Transactions
docs.text:
async with repo.transaction() as session:
    await (UpdateBuilder(repo.collection, doc_id, session=session)
        .set(Product.price, 29.99)
        .execute()
    )

docs.title: Result
docs.text: .execute() returns the updated document dict or None if not found.
